newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica to cut 3,700 jobs, take charge.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica to cut 3,700 jobs, take charge.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp said Thursday it would cut about 3,700 jobs in 1997 and take a pre-tax charge of $280 million in a restructuring of its business activities.
It said the charge will result in a $165 million reduction in net income in the fourth quarter.
"We are changing our business mix in both Europe and Japan based on changing markets, and we are streamlining our operations activities around the world," Chairman David Coulter said in a statement.
"We expect that almost all of these restructurings will be accomplished in 1997 and that the charge will be recovered in cost savings by the end of 1998," he said.
The company said it will be reducing staff and restructuring units in "mature" European markets while expanding activities in emerging European markets.

In Japan, charges relate to a previously announced restructuring of the Tokyo branch's activities and anticipated staff reductions caused by reduced demand for traditional credit products there, BankAmerica said.

It said it will close about 120 branches in California during 1997 while adding to other retail services. BankAmerica currently operates about 1,400 retail outlets, as well as 3,800 ATMs, in California.

"Eliminating positions is always difficult," Coulter said. "However, we have learned that it is better to take such action when the company is performing well, as BankAmerica is today. For instance, the likelihood of placing employees in other positions is better in good circumstances."
